biography.plain_text: Tommy "Mbogo" Allen is an American explorer, strategist and founder of Five Oceans, a non-profit supporting marine research and conservation. He later shifted towards ocean science, maritime archaeology and coastal programmes intended to strengthen environmental and economic resilience.

long_biography.plain_text:
A 1972 journey through Kenya, Yemen and North Africa shaped Tommy "Mbogo" Allen's life as an expedition leader. Encounters with Wilfred Thesiger and photographer Peter Beard encouraged him to learn local languages and approach travel through the communities he met. He later crossed northern Kenya on foot, walked the Chalbi and Kalahari deserts, and followed Somalia's Juba and Shebelle rivers towards the Indian Ocean.

Allen became a Fellow of the Explorers Club and has used his African regional experience in humanitarian and environmental work. His expeditions have combined mapping, photography and practical technology, including a satellite link used to seek medical guidance for a child with a snakebite in northern Kenya. Five Oceans now gives that field discipline an institutional home in research, conservation and coastal initiatives.
